name: Sam Ochoa
life: “I still remember carrying a wounded gull to a cardboard box.” Tuesday often includes a stop at Juniper Street, where Sam knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I want him to keep feeding the gull with the broken foot. I didn't think to ask who would feed him.
appearance: Sam has a dark undercut with a longer wave on top, heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw, and a favorite piece of clothing, an olive canvas jacket. It usually goes with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. When somebody else has the floor, Sam leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations.
personality: Sam gets protective of anybody who comes into a meeting unprepared. Sam privately wishes people would notice the amount of preparation behind this apparent ease.
agenda: To arrange food for the person who looks after the gull.
family: Bruna Andrade is Sam’s first cousin once removed. Sam brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Bruna makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *An address in pencil*, Bruna says, “I wrote the figure the way Dad did and nobody under thirty could read it.”
connections: Sasha Gil. A departing berth holder is still somebody a dock neighbor is counting on to feed a gull.

reactions.situation: A friend offers a sofa for an uncertain number of weeks
reactions.response: Sam agrees a first review date for the sofa without pretending it settles the winter.

reactions.response: Sam writes down their exact words with room left for uncertainty and gives them back to check.
